# Data Table layout

The examples below show some possible approaches to setup responsive <LinkTo kind="Components/DataTable" story="basic">Data Table</LinkTo> layouts.<br />
The component is built to take 100% width and height of the parent html element.<br />

## Fixed layout

The simplest way of adapting the Data Table size is by using fixed width and height values if it fits the design of your application.<br />
Using [Media Queries](https://www.w3schools.com/css/css_rwd_mediaqueries.asp) makes it possible to adapt the size to different devices or screen sizes.<br />
In this example, we use css transitions to show how the component adapts.

<Canvas of={DataTableTemplateStories.FixedLayout} />

```css
.datatable-fixed-example { transition: width 2s, height 2s; }
.w-288 { width: 288px; }  
.pb-1 { padding-bottom: 1rem; }
```

## Fluid layout

In real life applications, you would generally have to setup a css layout so that the parent element of the Data Table has a dynamic height based on a region of the screen.
CSS [Flexbox](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_flexible_box_layout/Basic_concepts_of_flexbox) or [Grid Layout](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout/Basic_concepts_of_grid_layout) can help (see https://caniuse.com/css-grid for compatibility).<br />

This example demonstrates a simple Grid Layout (2x2) to simulate a page with a fixed Side Nav and Header, and a fluid Data Table with a maximum width.

<Canvas of={DataTableTemplateStories.FluidLayout} />

```css
.gridlayout-example-root {
  width: 100vw;
  height: 100vh;
  overflow: hidden;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 128px minmax(100px, auto);
  grid-template-rows: 56px minmax(100px, auto);
  gap: 0.25rem;
  text-align: center;
}
.gridlayout-example-side { grid-column: 1; grid-row-end: span 2; border: 1px dashed blue; }
.gridlayout-example-top { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 1; border: 1px dashed blue; }
.gridlayout-example-datatable { grid-column: 2; grid-row: 2; max-width: 900px; }
```
